pp:ce:2002:q3.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ce:2002:q3.question:
The following function has a local minima at which value of $x$?
$f(x)=x\sqrt{5-x^{2}}$

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} f\left ( x \right )&=x\sqrt{5-x^{2}} \\ {f}'\left ( x \right )&=\sqrt{5-x^{2}}+\frac{x\times -2x}{2\sqrt{5-x^{2}}} \\ 5-x^{2}&=x^{2} \\ 2x^{2}&=5 \\ x&=\pm \sqrt{\frac{5}{2}}\end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q15.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 15
pp:ce:2002:q15.question: The force 'F' required at equilibrium on the semi-cylindrical gate shown below is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Hydrostatic Forces
detailed_solution.markdown:
Depth of water (H)=2 m

Consider unit width, of cylinder,

$$\begin{aligned} F_{H} &=\rho g \bar{h} A_{h} \\ &=1000 \times 9.81 \times\left(\frac{2}{2}\right) \times(2 \times 1) \\ &=19.62 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \text { width } \end{aligned}$$

Vertical component,

$$\begin{aligned} F_{v}&=\rho g(\text { volume })\\ &=1000 \times 9.81\left(\frac{\pi R^{2}}{2} \times 1\right) \\ &=15.41 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \text { width } \end{aligned}$$

location of center of pressure of $F_{h}$

$h^{*}=\frac{2}{3} H=\frac{4}{3} m$

location of center of pressure of $F_{v}$

$\therefore \quad \bar{x}=\frac{4 R}{3 \pi}=\frac{4 \times 1}{3 \pi}=0.424 \mathrm{m}$

Moment about hinge,

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad F_{H} \times\left(h^{*}-\bar{h}\right)&=F_{V} \times \bar{x}+F \times 1 \\ \therefore 19.62 \times\left(\frac{4}{3}-1\right)&=15.41 \times 0.424+F \times 1 \\ \therefore \quad F&=0 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q16.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 16
pp:ce:2002:q16.question:
Velocity distribution in a boundary layer flow over a plate is given by
$(u/u_{m})=1.5 \eta$
where, $\eta =y/\delta$; y is the distance measured normal to the plate; $\delta$ is the boundary layer thickness; and $u_m$ is the maximum velocity at $y =\delta$. If the shear stress $\tau$, acting on the plate is given by
$\tau =K(\mu u_{m})\delta$
where, $\mu$ is the dynamic viscosity of the fluid, K takes the value of

primary.subtopicLabel: Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \text { Given, } \frac{u}{u_{m}}=1.5 \eta ; \; \; &\;\eta=\frac{y}{\delta} \\ \therefore \quad u &=1.5 u_{m} \times \frac{y}{\delta} \\ \frac{d u}{d y} &=1.5 \frac{u_{m}}{\delta} \\ \text { Now, }\quad \tau&=\mu \frac{d u}{d y}=1.5 \mu \frac{u_{m}}{\delta} \\ \therefore \quad k &=1.5 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q26.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 26
pp:ce:2002:q26.question:
The value of the following improper integral is
$\int_{0}^{1}xlnx$

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \int_{0}^{1}x\log xdx&=\log x\int_{0}^{1}xdx-\int_{0}^{1}\left ( \frac{1}{x}\int xdx \right )dx \\   &=\frac{x^{2}}{2}\log x-\int_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x}\frac{x^{2}}{2}dx \\   &=\left [ \frac{x^{2}}{2}\log x-\frac{x^{2}}{4} \right ]^{1}_{0} \\   &=\left ( 0-\frac{1}{4} \right )-\left ( 0-0 \right )=-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q27.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 27

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} f\left (x,y \right )&=x^{2}+y^{2} \\ \triangledown f&=2xi+2yi \\ \triangledown f&=2i+4j \\ e&=\frac{4i+3j}{5}\\ D\cdot D&=\triangledown f\cdot e\\ D\cdot D&=\frac{8+12}{5}=4 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q29.question:
The limit of the following sequence as n $\rightarrow \infty$ is
$x_n=n^{1/n}$

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} l&=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty }n^{1/n} \\ \log l&=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty }\log n^{1/n} \\  &=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty }\frac{1}{n}\log n&=\frac{\infty }{\infty }\\ &\text{by L-Hospital's rules,}\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow \infty }\frac{1/n}{1}&=\frac{1}{\infty }=0 \\ \log l&=0 \\ l&=e^{0}=1\end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q35.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:ce:2002:q35.question:
An infinite slope is to be constructed in a soil. The effective stress strength
parameters of the soil are c'=0 and ${\phi}' =30^{\circ}$. The saturated unit weight of the

of safety of 1.5 would be

pp:ce:2002:q37.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 37
pp:ce:2002:q37.question:
The time for a clay layer to achieve 85% consolidation is 10 years. If the layer was
half as thick, 10 times more permeable and 4 times more compressible then the
time that would be required to achieve the same degree of consolidation is

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} k &=C_{v} m_{v} \gamma_{w} \\ T_{v} &=\frac{C_{v} t}{h^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad \text { and } \quad t_{1} &=\frac{h_{1}^{2} T_{v}}{k_{1}} m_{v} \gamma_{w} \\ \therefore \quad & t_{2}=\frac{h_{2}^{2} T_{v}}{k_{2}} m_{v} \gamma_{w} \\ & \frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}=\left(\frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}}\right)^{2} \times \frac{T_{v}}{T_{v}} \times \frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}} \times \frac{m_{v 1}}{m_{v 2}}\\ \frac{t_{2}}{t_{1}} &=\left(\frac{h_{2}}{h_{1}}\right)^{2} \times \frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}} \times \frac{m_{v 2}}{m_{v 1}} \\ &=\frac{1}{4} \times 1 \times \frac{1}{10} \times 4=\frac{1}{10} \\ t_{2} &=\frac{t_{1}}{10}=\frac{10}{10}=1 \text { year } \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q38.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ce:2002:q38.question:
In a triaxial test carried out on a cohesionless soil sample with a cell pressure of
20 kPa, the observed value of applied stress at the point of failure was 40 kPa.
The angle of internal friction of the soil is

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shear Strength of Soil
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Given,}\quad \sigma_{1} &=\sigma_{a}+\sigma_{3} \\ &=40+20=60 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \text{Now,}\quad \sigma_{1} &=\sigma_{3} N_{0}+2 \mathrm{c} \sqrt{\mathrm{N}_{2}}\\ \text{Where }\quad c&=0\\ \frac{\sigma_{1}}{\sigma_{3}} &=N_{0}=\frac{60}{20}=3 \\ &=\tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\\ \tan \left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)&=\sqrt{3}=1.732 \\ 45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}&=60^{\circ} \\ \text{or }\quad \frac{\phi}{2}&=60^{\circ}-45^{\circ} \\ \phi&=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}\\$$

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Infiltration, Runoff and Hydrographs

W-index $=\frac{P-Q}{t}=\frac{\left ( 3+8+12+6+2 \right )-15}{5} =3.2 cm/day$

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} Q &=432\; m^{3}/hr \\ V_{s} &=0.12\; cm/s \\ &=0.0012\; m/s \\ \text{Area} &=\frac{432/3600}{0.0012}...\text{to remove 100\% particles} \\ &=100\; m^{2} \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ To remove 90% of particles

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &=100\times 0.9 \\ &=90\; m^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q46.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:ce:2002:q46.question: The theoretical oxygen demand of a 0.001 mol/L glucose solution is

primary.subtopicLabel: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
$1\: mol\: of\: glucose\rightarrow 6\: moles\: of\: O_{2}$

$0.001\: \frac{mol}{l}\: of\: glucose\rightarrow 0.006\: \frac{mol}{l}\: of\: O_{2}$

Now, number of moles

$$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{Wt\left ( g \right )}{Molecular\: Wt\left ( g \right )} \\ \therefore \; \; \text{Wt} &=0.006\times 32 \\ &=0.192\: g/l \\ &=192\; mg/l \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2002:q47.title: GATE CE 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 47
pp:ce:2002:q47.question:
A wastewater sample has an initial BOD of 222 mg/L. The first order BOD decay
coefficient is 0.4/day. The BOD consumed (in mg/L) in 5 days is

primary.subtopicLabel: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
BOD consumed

$$\begin{aligned} &=BOD_{u}\left [ 1-e^{kt} \right ] \\ &=222\left [ 1-e^{-0.4\times 5} \right ] \\ &= 191.95\; mg/l\simeq 192\: mg/l \end{aligned}$$
